newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX heat ends with rally again, boosted by APIs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX heat ends with rally again, boosted by APIs.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil rallied for the second straight session Thursday after oil inventory data failed to show a significant build in low heating oil supplies amid unseasonably cold weather in large portions of the United States.
"We are in a strong buying mode. There are low heating oil supplies when it is a lot colder in the Midwest and East Coast," said James Cordier, a trader with Allendale Inc.
December heating oil settled a sharp 2.20 cents higher at 73.40 cents a gallon. Heating oil boosted December crude which ended up 29 cents at $24.41 a barrel.
December gasoline ended 0.58 cent up at 68.92 cents a gallon.
"The APIs were obviously extremely supportive," said a trader.
On Wednesday, the American Petroleum Institute (API) said distillate stocks, which includes heating oil and deisel, fell 827,000 barrels for the week ended November 8.
Heating oil stocks grew a meager 120,000 barrels, with growth restrained by increased demand last week in preparation for this week's cold spell in the U.S. Northeast, dealers said.

Weather Services Corp forecasted temperatures will continue to be eight to 15 degrees below normal in the Northeast and below normal in the Midwest as well. However, temperatures are expected to moderate to normal by next week in both regions.
The heating oil-to-crude crack spread widened to $6.42 a barrel Thursday from $5.34 a barrel Monday.
Traders said the forecast for warmer temperatures could trigger profit-taking in the oil complex in the next two sessions.
"You could see some profit-taking later in tommorow's session," said Allendale's Cordier.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
